Vowel reduction

See what happens to every syllable you did not lean on.

The rule

In the lesson on Word Stress, you.learned that the stressed syllable is higher, stronger, longer. Every other syllable in the word is lower, weaker and shorter, and its vowel collapses.

Lean on one part of the word. Swallow the rest.
It's like a double gymnastic. Two moves, not one.

Putting the accent on is the easy half, and most people do it. Then they say the other syllables at full strength, carefully and clearly, and the word still sounds French. The swallowing is the half that makes it English, and it feels wrong to do, because it feels like mumbling. It is not mumbling. It is the language.

Reduction is a result, not a rule

1 · Where the vowel lands

A swallowed vowel does not disappear into silence. It lands on one of two sounds

nothingThe schwa The sound named after nothing. Most swallowed vowels land here, whatever letter is written.
actor dangerous sensor signal banana
SEN-suh · SIG-nul · buh-NAH-nuh
a short iThe short i The other landing place, and the one nobody expects.
village ticket circuit minute orange
SIR-kit · MIN-it · ORR-inj

2 · The double gymnastic

Two moves on every word. First find the syllable you lean on. Then say where the swallowed one lands. Both are scored.

Word 1 of 0
 

In each pair the extra syllable is barely audible, and it is still a different word.

dress / addressuh-DRESS
drive / driverDRY-vuh
office / officerOFF-iss-uh
way / awayuh-WAY
women / womanWIM-in / WUM-uhn

Now the same trick on some technical vocabulary. Each pair is one swallowed syllable apart, and in every case the new syllable is the -or that lands on nothing.

resist / resistorri-ZIST / ri-ZIST-uh
connect / connectorcuh-NECT / cuh-NECT-uh
generate / generatorJEN-uh-rate / JEN-uh-ray-tuh
conduct / conductorcuhn-DUCT / cuhn-DUCT-uh

4 · Say it

Lean on the capitals. Everything not in capitals should be shorter and quieter

The sensor sends a signal to the connector. 🔊 Listen
A resistor, a capacitor, a generator. 🔊 Listen
Circuit, minute, voltage. 🔊 Listen

Three short i's where you expected something else: SER-kit, MIN-it, VOL-tij. The spelling never changes, only the vowel you give it.

Read it slowly, then at speed.

Little Miss Muffet,
Sat on a tuffet,
Eating her curds and whey;
Along came a spider,
Who sat down beside her,
And frightened Miss Muffet away.
